contract: Stream-sync run end: outcome, covered streams, checkpoint candidate and whole streams from host observations (planRunFinish).
source: Ported from the Desktop host's planner (covered streams with source answers, safe checkpoints, the finish plan, and the retry rule that withholds cursors of unsent records), which this replaces.
capture: What the connector emitted, in protocol terms: records per stream (key, op), SKIP_RESULT (stream absent = run-wide; retryable as the runtime decides), DETAIL_GAP (retryable unless it said retryable:false), DETAIL_COVERAGE reports, reports the host refused, streams the host refused before sending, and the streams a failed DONE named failed. input.streams is the observation every host must map that capture to.

cases.why: Every stream answered: succeeded, every cursor moves.
A skipped stream is not covered and keeps its cursor.
A silent incremental stream is covered and its cursor moves.
A silent stream this run would clear is not covered.
An explicit delete answers for a full-refresh stream.
A whole-stream proof answers for an empty full-refresh stream.
A full-refresh run where no stream answered confirms nothing and fails.
Records fold by key in order: a re-upsert after a delete leaves a live record.
Records fold by key in order: an upsert deleted later in the same run leaves no live record, and the delete still answers the stream.
A retry run covers nothing; streams with captured records keep their cursor, record-free tokens move.
A retry run with no records keeps every safe cursor.
g <- p <- c and p <- d: an unsent child holds every ancestor, and a held parent drops its other children.
c depends on p and q; an unsent p drops c but never q.
An unsent parent drops its children's cursors.
An unsent child withholds its parent's cursor too.
A retry run's explicit deletes still count, but the stream is not covered and keeps its cursor.
A retryable skip makes the run retry; an other skip blocks that stream's cursor.
A retryable skip of a record-free stream keeps that stream's job token.
A skip that names no stream skips every stream: nothing confirmed, the run fails.
A run that confirmed nothing still keeps its explicit deletes, and moves no cursor.
z <- m <- a: a skipped grandchild blocks its parent and grandparent, transitively.
c depends on p and q; p emitted no cursor, so c loses its own, and q keeps its own.
A detail report short of whole holds the parent's cursor, and the child's with it.
A whole detail report naming the parent lets both cursors move.
A required key the report did not hydrate holds the parent.
A report naming another STATE stream holds the declared parent.
With no declared parent the stream is its own parent: no report holds its own cursor.
A stream with a detail gap is not covered; outside a retry a fatal gap does not block other cursors.
A retryable detail gap on a parent blocks it and prunes its child.
Any detail gap on a declared parent blocks the parent's cursor.
Under a retry a fatal detail gap blocks that stream's cursor.
A stream the host refused before sending is skipped: not covered, cursor held.
An invalid detail report does not uncover the stream, but holds its cursor.
Only covered streams are named whole.
A cursor for a stream the run did not cover never moves.
A certified failed DONE keeps the healthy streams' records, names them whole, and moves no cursor.
A failed child holds its healthy parent; nothing is left to keep, so the run fails.
A certified failed DONE with only a healthy cursor still ends partial, keeping nothing.
A coverage report short of whole keeps the stream's records but never names it whole.
A certified failed DONE that names no failed stream counts as upsert-only.
An uncertified failed DONE keeps the records of unskipped streams, names nothing whole, moves no cursor.
An uncertified failed DONE never covers a stream DONE named failed, even one with records and no skip.
An uncertified failed DONE whose only records belong to a stream DONE named failed keeps nothing: the run failed.
A failed DONE with nothing to keep fails.
A failed DONE with only a delete keeps it.
A stream named failed in DONE is never covered, even when it also sent an explicit delete. Run end still keeps that delete; packages/server/src/localdb/run-end.test.ts asserts it.
A child whose parent this run did not select keeps no cursor.
A run that selected no stream has nothing to confirm: it succeeds and moves no cursor.
